#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Hook: PostToolUse
# Name: my-custom-hook
#
# Runs after a tool call completes. Reads the hook event JSON from stdin
# and reports approve/block/non-blocking-error via exit code.
#
# Exit codes:
#   0 - success / approve (stdout may carry JSON for hook-specific fields)
#   1 - non-blocking error (stderr shown to user, tool result still applies)
#   2 - blocking error (stderr shown to Claude, treated as failure)

set -euo pipefail

if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "my-custom-hook: jq is required but not installed" >&2
  exit 1
fi

input="$(cat)"

tool_name="$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.tool_name // empty')"
tool_input="$(echo "$input" | jq -c '.tool_input // {}')"
tool_response="$(echo "$input" | jq -c '.tool_response // {}')"

# TODO: custom logic goes here

exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Claude Code hook: PostToolUse
# Runs after a tool call completes. Receives hook event JSON on stdin.
set -euo pipefail

if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "my-custom-hook: jq is required but not installed" >&2
  exit 1
fi

input="$(cat)"

tool_name="$(jq -r '.tool_name // empty' <<<"$input")"
tool_input="$(jq -c '.tool_input // {}' <<<"$input")"
tool_response="$(jq -c '.tool_response // {}' <<<"$input")"

# TODO: custom logic here — inspect $tool_name / $tool_input / $tool_response
# and act on the completed tool call.

# Exit codes:
#   0 - success; stdout shown to user in transcript mode, does not block
#   2 - blocking error; stderr is fed back to Claude as feedback
#   *  - other non-zero; non-blocking error, stderr shown to user only
exit 0

files.lint-output.txt:
Hook Lint Report
File: bad-hook.json

[FAIL] Overly broad matcher
  matcher: ".*"
  This regex matches every tool name, so the hook fires on ALL tool
  calls (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, WebFetch, etc.) instead of a specific
  tool or narrow set. Broad matchers cause unnecessary hook invocations,
  hidden side effects on unrelated tools, and make intent hard to audit.
  Fix: scope the matcher to the intended tool(s), e.g. "Bash" or
  "Write|Edit".

[WARN] Command references a world-writable temp path
  command: "bash /tmp/x.sh"
  /tmp/x.sh is not version-controlled and can be modified by any local
  process/user before the hook runs. Prefer a script path inside the
  project or plugin directory.

Result: 1 FAIL, 1 WARN

Hook Lint Report: bad-hook.json

[FAIL] Overly broad matcher
  matcher: ".*"
  command: "bash /tmp/x.sh"
  Issue: ".*" matches every tool call (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, WebFetch, etc.),
  not a specific tool. This runs the hook command on ALL tool use, which is
  almost certainly unintended and a security/performance risk (arbitrary
  command fires unconditionally on every action).
  Fix: scope matcher to the intended tool name(s), e.g. "Bash" or
  "Write|Edit", instead of the catch-all ".*".

Result: 1 issue found (1 fail, 0 warnings).
